transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, to be honest, I'm quite embarrassed to be here, but I’ll sit down to eat and end up putting away way more food than anyone else, more than I ever planned. It really scares me how much I'm eating, and I just don't know why I can't seem to stop myself.
After these overeating episodes, do you ever try to make up for it by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?

It's very hard to admit, but after a big meal I've gone into the bathroom to make myself throw up or taken extra laxatives to get it out. Other days, I'll force myself to skip breakfast and lunch, or walk laps around the block until my legs ache just to work off the food. I just feel I have to do it so it doesn't hurt my heart or make me gain weight.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes recurrent binge-eating episodes with loss of control and repeated compensatory behaviors, including self-induced vomiting, laxative misuse, fasting, and excessive exercise, driven by fear of weight gain. This is most consistent with bulimia nervosa.
